label: Verve
rationale: Penguin Guide Core Collection with a crown accolade — 'one of the great modern jazz records.' A pianoless standards trio where the cool-school alto master meets Elvin Jones's polyrhythmic drive on the eve of the Coltrane quartet; the seam between cool-jazz lyricism and incoming post-bop rhythm. Bridge case: for a listener coming from the composed canon, Motion shows how a full-frontal rhythm section frees a linear improviser — the heads are fragments, the time is elastic, and Konitz's behind-the-beat phrasing is the cool aesthetic taken to its interactive extreme.
scope_flag: cool-jazz leader with post-bop drummer; stylistic boundary record on the cool-to-post-bop seam
bridge_case: Pianoless trio with Elvin Jones: the cool-jazz tradition encountering the new 1961 rhythmic language; teaches how interactive drumming transforms standards improvisation.

ballot.case_for: Session gravity is the load-bearing signal: the cool school's supreme linear improviser, stripped of piano and arranging scaffolding, recorded on August 29, 1961 with Elvin Jones at the precise moment Jones was remaking jazz time inside the Coltrane quartet — a genuinely productive collision, with Sonny Dallas as the connective bassist (S1–S3, all obs). The pianoless format forces Konitz into total linear exposure and turns well-worn standards ('I Remember You,' 'All of Me,' 'You'd Be So Nice to Come Home To') into elastic, interactive dialogues that anticipate the freer standards treatments of the mid-to-late 1960s. Per the dossier rationale and Ref 2, the record carries Penguin Guide Core Collection status with a rare Crown accolade — 'one of the great modern jazz records' — and reads as Konitz's defining leader statement; it passes the discovery test, the friction between dry astringent alto and Jones's cross-rhythms still sounding daring rather than academic.
ballot.case_against: The consensus pillar is asserted, not evidenced: the Penguin crown claim lives only in the dossier's prose while S1–S6 are metadata databases (AllMusic, Wikipedia, Discogs, iTunes, MusicBrainz, Cover Art Archive) with no critical-press or musician-testimony source — the exact signal the for-case leans on is unverified. Motion is not obviously the right Konitz entry: the defining-record argument arguably belongs to Subconscious-Lee and the Tristano-era material, and nothing in the dossier argues why this title outperforms the more canonical alternatives. The program is five standards in strict head-and-solos form with no compositional or formal innovation, and the 'cool-to-post-bop seam' framing overstates the record — Konitz sounds like Konitz over Jones, a respected configuration rather than a genre pivot.
ballot.recommendation: John should hold Motion as a contested, strong-priority candidate and have the Penguin Guide Core Collection/Crown claim verified against the guide itself (3rd/4th ed.) before deciding — if it verifies, the case tightens materially toward consensus_core, and he should weigh in the same pass whether Motion or Subconscious-Lee is the right first Konitz entry.
